title: Why the architect needs to keep writing code

videos.script: Renata estimated two weeks. The team said six. {{estimate}} She offered to pair for an afternoon, to show them how small the change was. The test suite took forty-one minutes. The framework had moved on. The deploy needed another team's review. {{afternoon}} The team was right, and she had stopped being able to tell. This lesson is about why an architect keeps writing code. It is not to be the best programmer in the building. It is to stay calibrated, so the next design is priced correctly. {{calibration}} Then, which code. Nothing a release waits for, because an architect's week is full of interruptions. Spikes, prototypes, a walking skeleton, fitness functions, small fixes. And pairing on the hard parts, instead of owning them. {{map}} Last, how to keep the habit when every meeting looks more urgent. Protected time, work you can finish, and review from the team like anybody else. {{habit}} At the end there are five questions to ask yourself once a month, to notice the drift before the team does.
